mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation models, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In any 3-year rolling window, the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% from the prior month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increases in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as manufacturing weakness signals an impending recession, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor in recessionary conditions is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.0%) indicates a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profit growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In any 3-year rolling window, the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03, or the average 20-day return when UNRATE < 5.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% from the prior month signals rising inflation, which triggers expectations of monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 0.3% month-over-month, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST increase and RSAFS increase does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 8.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the weak labor market suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 8.0%, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor in high unemployment regimes is less than 0.03.
